title: Model Compression: Pruning, Quantization, Distillation
overview: Compression makes models smaller and faster for deployment. Pruning removes weights, quantization lowers numeric precision and distillation trains a small student to mimic a larger teacher.
objectives: Quantize weights to int8 with a scale

method.title: Pruning
method.body: Remove weights with small magnitude (unstructured) or whole channels and heads (structured), usually followed by fine-tuning.

method.title: Quantization
method.body: Map float weights to low-bit integers using a scale; post-training or quantization-aware training trades a little accuracy for memory and speed.

method.title: Distillation
method.body: The student matches the teacher's temperature-softened output distribution, optionally with the true labels.

method.title: Trade-offs
method.body: Structured sparsity and int8 usually give real speedups, while unstructured sparsity needs hardware support.

pseudocode:
# int8 quantization
scale = max(abs(w)) / 127
q = round(w / scale).clip(-128, 127)
w_hat = q * scale
# distillation
loss = KL(softmax(t/T), softmax(s/T)) * T**2 + ce(s, y)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
w = rng.normal(size=1000).astype(np.float32)
scale = np.abs(w).max() / 127
q = np.clip(np.round(w / scale), -128, 127).astype(np.int8)
w_hat = q.astype(np.float32) * scale
print("max quantization error:", round(float(np.abs(w - w_hat).max()), 4))
thr = np.quantile(np.abs(w), 0.5)
pruned = np.where(np.abs(w) >= thr, w, 0)
print("sparsity after pruning:", round(float((pruned == 0).mean()), 2))
